title: Actual nextAttack/setTargetPlayer/advanceGF active-display reception v50

reused_harness.boundary: Only factory declarations before v48 case generation are evaluated;no old archive is rewritten. Actual helpers execute in a fresh pinned client VM.

methods: ks.k complete nextAttack,setTargetPlayer,advanceGF branches with synchronous Future shell
fs.fu/aa actual frame build/clear;fv.fq actual fresh caller;fv.aT actual target-pane update
h8.u/J actual roster lookup;fs.a6/aO actual model-column access
dA.iI/gf2 actual summary and v48 public card numeric projection
projection_scope: Roster IDs/GF/panes/selection/active summary and drawn card values only;not board resources,hand,curse,guardian effects,actor/server phase,controls,animations or timers.
conclusions: Incremental nextAttack invokes fu after source lookup,clears both panes/selection/product/old frame,and draws source plus the supplied column. It doesnot replay the fresh-only positive target/buying restoration. Even unknown positive rawtarget is ignored by this incremental branch.

setTargetPlayer performs a real roster lookup even for ID0. aT selecting the current source only highlights sourceSide;it doesnot clear the old opposite player or commodity card. A different target updates the opposite pane while preserving a drawn commodity.

advanceGF calls actual aa,which resets orientation/panes/selection/old frame,then increments GF and looks up the supplied player for the left source pane. Unknown event player can therefore throw after client partial clear/increment. Native atomic rejection is a separate adapter guarantee.

Fresh isOver initialization skips turn/source/target lookups and leaves the newly constructed active display empty. The examined nextAttack and advanceGF event branches have no equivalent ending gate and can update that display afterward.

A target event on a completely empty ending display can update a pane/selection before later overlay code dereferences the missing source. Core pane changes and complete-handler visual errors are therefore recorded separately. Native partial display projection is not an emulator of those overlay failures.
No event is generated here. The supplied sequence determines every update;there is no RNG,server damage,recipient selection,copy/gift policy,phase transition or implicit action.
limitations: This report tests a bounded display reducer,not Match import/replay or an authoritative event stream. Initial fresh construction uses spectator/no-Fog/no-Flash board shells;hand/resources/UID/rating/control widgets and timed visual overlays are outside scope.

Complete handler errors retain the actual final-or-partial display in JSON for diagnosis. ERROR TSV rows indicate native whole-batch rejection and do NOT assert that the browser rolled back its earlier visual changes.
The adapter rejects unsafe GF+1 and invalid knownmodel fields even when that raw field would remain undrawn. These strict-domain extensions are labeled separately from actual handler lookup failures.

For a full-handler error after successful core pane update,the expected native JSON represents only that completed core projection. Following events are not invented after a failed handler in these fixtures.

The v48 attack serializer semantics are retained except target comes from current selected pane and an already drawn commodity persists across T events. Neither rawunusedscalar nor a future model/event queue is exposed.
The reused factory and helper hashes are pinned;no client source text is embedded in the report. No applicationstartup,network/account,timer,C++engine/build or existing source/report edits run.
